_note: The floor of the Wextreen Sump. Water on every side and an island in the middle of it, and the way back up is the way you came. The door onto the Undercountry is added in M14.4, with the map it opens onto. **No `outside`**: a floor of the Sump is not one sitting, because its budget is what you brought rather than how tired you are. A save taken here reopens here, and a player who needs a three-by-two from the van can go and get it; what that costs is the walk. **And nothing here names an instrument** — `reach.rs::nothing_in_a_map_file_knows_about_a_survey` refuses one, and it is right to: a map that knew which lens reads it is a map that would have to be edited to add a second. **Floored with `road`, like every other dungeon in this game.** The first draft floored all eight of these with `scrub` — 140 per mille against a pool this strong is a fight every four steps, and `make play` wore a level-twenty board to the sixty percent cap crossing one room and went home. The Cave, the Stack and the map under the lake are all cut passages floored with road at 30, and a floor whose walk costs more than its puzzle is a floor that is a corridor with a toll on it.

places.name: the door onto the Undercountry
places.shut: The door is cut for two hands and has two keyholes in it, and one of them turns.
prose: Both of them turn. The door goes back nine inches and stops against something soft, and the something soft is grass.
There is a country on the other side of it, and the other way in comes out four miles west of this one. Somebody cut both and did not mention either.
